name: IA-04
label: Safe R

key_factors: Open seat after Feenstra's retirement, removing incumbent effects
Republican McGowan's large fundraising edge over Democrat Dawson
Prediction markets price about 95% for Republicans
model.rationale: This northwest Iowa seat is deeply Republican, and the open-seat dynamic does not change that: McGowan has outraised Dawson roughly five-to-one and holds a cash advantage, while markets price the race at about 95% Republican. With no polls available, the forecast rests on the district's lean and fundamentals, keeping the margin near R+15.
model.watch: A competitive or divisive Republican primary that leaves McGowan damaged, or a late Democratic funding surge, could narrow the margin.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Randy Feenstra (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Iowa's 4th District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the state, and incumbent Randy Feenstra's retirement to run for governor leaves it open but still firmly on the GOP side of the map. No general-election polls are available, so the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean and candidate fundamentals.

Republican Chris McGowan has raised about $680,000 with outside support behind him, while Democrat David Dawson has raised roughly $136,000 with little cash on hand. Prediction markets give Republicans about a 95% chance of holding the seat. The race is rated Likely Republican, with the main uncertainty coming from the open-seat nature of the contest and the absence of polling.
